subject: Proposal: Multi-Quarter Price Lock with Usage Staircase & Earned Credits
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@solarity.io>, procurement@solarity.io
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Proposal: Multi-Quarter Price Lock with Usage Staircase & Earned Credits

Hi Elena / Solarity procurement team,

Following up on our renewal window — thanks again for the candid conversation last week about your expected product-led usage ramp. Based on your guidance (25% q/q growth through H1), I put together a proposal that balances price stability for Solarity with a growth-friendly commit structure from Redwood. High-level: 

- 12% list discount on current rates applied as a price-protection corridor for the first 3 quarters after signature.
- Staggered committed-usage bands (staircase): baseline commit this quarter, +20% commit in Q2, +40% commit in Q3; actual invoicing will use realized usage but credits apply as described below.
- Earned credits: if realized usage exceeds committed band by >=10% in any quarter, Solarity receives an earned credit equal to 7% of that quarter's invoice (credit applied on next invoice).
- SLA credit: standard SLA (99.9%) with operational credits; we can expand this in the contract if you need a stricter SLA.

I attached a short proposal and a mutual action plan (MAP) deck that outlines milestones and signatures. If this aligns, I can pull finance and legal into a short call to convert to a term sheet.

Attachments: 20270210-solarity-price-lock-proposal.pdf (proposal summary)

Next steps I suggest:
- Can you confirm target signature window (you mentioned mid-March)?
- Procurement: any must-have contracting language or approvals we should include early?

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call tomorrow to walk through the MAP.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
mateo@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0162

From: Elena Park <elena@solarity.io>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@solarity.io
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal: Multi-Quarter Price Lock with Usage Staircase & Earned Credits

Mateo — thanks for the clear proposal and the MAP. A couple of initial asks from procurement and legal: 

1) Price-hold length: procurement is pushing for a price hold for at least 6 quarters (we're trying to avoid re-budgeting mid-year). Is there flexibility to extend the corridor?
2) SLA / credit floor: our legal team would like a more prescriptive SLA-credit schedule if availability drops below 99.9% (we can share a template).
3) Documentation: we need SOC 2 Type II evidence and data-retention commitments included before we escalate to our CPO.

Also — what does the earned credit arithmetic look like if usage spikes above committed bands dramatically in one quarter and then falls back? We need to understand true bill impact over rolling quarters.

If you can tighten the proposal on the two items above and include a 1-pager on how credits net across quarters, we can brief leadership next week. We do still want price predictability — so there's interest, but procurement is cautious on a short lock.

Thanks,
Elena Park
Head of Platform Partnerships | Solarity Systems
elena@solarity.io

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@solarity.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, procurement@solarity.io
Date: Fri, 12 Feb 2027 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal: Multi-Quarter Price Lock with Usage Staircase & Earned Credits

Elena — appreciate the details. Quoting your note below for context.

> Price-hold length: procurement is pushing for a price hold for at least 6 quarters...
> SLA / credit floor: legal wants a prescriptive SLA-credit schedule...
> Documentation: SOC 2 Type II evidence and data-retention commitments...

Counter-proposal (to surface internal approvals quickly):
- Firm price lock for 3 quarters from signature (covers Q2/Q3/Q4 operationally); thereafter a reviewed rate for Q5+ with a protected corridor (we're willing to negotiate an automatic extension if usage and payment cadence meet thresholds).
- Earned credit mechanics (simple): credits are calculated per quarter based on realized usage relative to that quarter's committed band. If usage > committed band by >=10%: credit = 7% of that quarter's invoice. Credits do not auto-expire; they apply to the next invoice and net across quarters (we cap accrued credits at 20% of a single-quarter invoice to avoid distortions). If usage spikes and then falls, credits remain earned for the quarter they were triggered — there is no retroactive clawback unless there's clear billing error.
- SLA: attach SLA-credit-terms.docx with a templated schedule; we can move to a higher SLA if you want a formal amendment.
- Documentation: we'll share SOC 2 Type II evidence and our data-retention policy link in the following email.

To expedite, I attached a draft MAP (MAP-Solarity-Q1Q2Q3.xlsx) with milestones (legal review, SOC 2 evidence, signature, onboarding dates). If this direction looks okay, Marissa (cc'd) can approve the commercial guardrails and loop in pricing/legal to create a single-term summary.

Attachments: MAP-Solarity-Q1Q2Q3.xlsx; SLA-credit-terms.docx

Would you be available Tues 2/16 for a 30-min alignment call?

Thanks,
Mateo
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@solarity.io>, procurement@solarity.io
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Feb 2027 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal: Multi-Quarter Price Lock with Usage Staircase & Earned Credits

Hi Elena / Solarity procurement — Mateo walked me through the background and your asks; thanks for being explicit on the 6-quarter preference. We want to be cooperative while protecting Redwood's ability to support the ramp. Finalized commercial direction from our side: 

1) Price hold: we can extend to a 4-quarter firm price lock from signature (instead of the 3-quarter counter) with a conditional extension clause to reach 6 quarters. The conditional extension triggers if Solarity meets the committed-band thresholds for two consecutive quarters and invoices are paid on time.

2) Additional timing incentive: if Solarity signs the term sheet by 2027-03-15, Redwood will add an additional one-time 4% loyalty discount on top of the corridor for the first renewal year. This is time-limited.

3) Earned credits: we agree with Mateo's calculation rules, with one clarification — credits will net against the following quarter invoice and a simple reconciliation statement will be provided with each invoice. Cap remains at 20% of a single-quarter invoice.

4) SLA and compliance: Redwood will provide SOC 2 Type II evidence and the data-retention matrix; SLA-credit schedule attached for legal review.

5) Next step: procurement, if you confirm you can accept the conditional-extension language we will issue a single-term summary and send via DocuSign for signature. Link: https://www.docusign.com/solar-quote/abc123. HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DL-2027-0553.

Attachments: approved-term-summary-20270217.pdf

If you want to accept the conditional extension and time-limited incentive, please reply and we'll route the DocuSign. Happy to join a call if you want any clarifying language.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0128
